title: Pinjore Gardens - A Beautiful Mughal Heritage Garden in Haryana
content:
Pinjore Gardens,

Pinjore Gardens, also known as Yadavindra Gardens, is one of the most famous and well-maintained historic gardens in North India. Located in the town of Pinjore near Panchkula, Haryana, this garden is a perfect blend of Mughal architecture, natural beauty, and royal history.

Surrounded by the Shivalik Hills, Pinjore Gardens is an ideal destination for families, couples, photographers, and history lovers. Its peaceful atmosphere, fountains, greenery, and symmetrical design make it a refreshing getaway from busy city life.

Historical Significance of Pinjore Gardens

Pinjore Gardens was built in the 17th century during the Mughal era. It is believed that the garden was designed by Fidai Khan, who was the architect of Emperor Aurangzeb.

Later, the garden was restored and maintained by the rulers of Patiala, and it was renamed Yadavindra Gardens in honor of Maharaja Yadavindra Singh.

The garden reflects the classic Mughal style of landscaping, where nature, water, and architecture come together beautifully.

Architecture and Layout

Pinjore Gardens is built in the traditional Mughal Charbagh pattern, meaning the garden is divided into symmetrical sections with flowing water channels.

The garden is spread across 7 terraced levels, each offering something unique. As visitors walk down from the top terrace to the lower levels, they experience a stunning view of fountains, flower beds, and historical structures.

Key architectural highlights include:

  • Beautiful gateways
  • Water fountains and canals
  • Royal pavilions
  • Terraced lawns

Major Attractions Inside Pinjore Gardens

  • Mughal Fountains and Water Channels: The most attractive feature of the garden is its long line of fountains running through the center. The flowing water adds calmness and charm to the entire environment.
  • Shish Mahal (Palace of Mirrors): Shish Mahal is a small palace structure inside the garden, once used by Mughal rulers. It adds a royal touch to the heritage beauty of the place.
  • Rang Mahal: Rang Mahal is another historical structure that was used for cultural events and royal gatherings.
  • Mini Zoo: Pinjore Gardens also has a small zoo area, which makes it enjoyable for children and families.
  • Japanese Garden: A beautifully designed Japanese-style garden is also present, adding an international charm to this historic site.

Pinjore Garden Light and Sound Show

One of the highlights of visiting Pinjore Gardens is the evening light and sound show. The illuminated fountains, colorful lights, and peaceful atmosphere make the garden look magical after sunset.

During festivals and special events, the garden becomes even more vibrant and lively.

Best Time to Visit Pinjore Gardens

  • October to March: Best weather for sightseeing and picnics
  • Spring season: Flowers are in full bloom
  • Evenings: Ideal for enjoying the lights and cool breeze

Avoid visiting during peak summer afternoons, as it can get hot.

How to Reach Pinjore Gardens

By Road- Pinjore is well connected and located near:

  • Chandigarh (approx. 22 km)
  • Panchkula (approx. 15 km)
  • Shimla highway (NH-5)

By Train: Nearest railway station: Chandigarh Railway Station

By Air: Nearest airport: Chandigarh International Airport

Entry Fee and Timings

Timings: 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM

Entry fees are affordable and may vary for adults and children.

(Visitors are advised to check updated ticket prices before visiting.)

Travel Tips

  • Visit in the evening for the best experience
  • Carry a camera for photography
  • Ideal spot for family picnics
  • Keep the garden clean and avoid plastic waste

Why You Should Visit Pinjore Gardens

Pinjore Gardens is not just a park; it is a historical masterpiece that reflects Mughal elegance and royal charm. It is a perfect destination for:

  • History and architecture lovers
  • Couples and photographers
  • Families looking for a peaceful outing
  • Travelers visiting Chandigarh or Panchkula
